regulator.name: Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur (RDI, formerly Agentschap Telecom)
regulator.document: Bijlage 1 'Radiozendamateurs' of the Regeling gebruik van frequentieruimte met meldingsplicht 2015 (implementing the Nationaal Frequentieplan 2018) - the frequency/power table the RDI amateur pages link to

source.name: Regeling gebruik van frequentieruimte met meldingsplicht 2015, Bijlage 1 (Radiozendamateurs)

note: Registration is licence-free but requires passing a CBR-run exam for category F (full, HAREC-equivalent) or N (novice, CEPT ECC/REC (05)06 level). The per-band assignments, power caps (W PEP) and primary/secondary status below are transcribed from Bijlage 1 of the Regeling gebruik van frequentieruimte met meldingsplicht 2015, the table the RDI (ex-Agentschap Telecom) amateur pages designate as the official frequency table implementing the Nationaal Frequentieplan 2018; the VERON band plan was kept as a cross-check fallback but was not needed since the primary table was retrievable. Class N is restricted to 40m, 20m and 10m plus 2m and 70cm with 100 W PEP on HF and 25 W PEP on VHF/UHF; class F has full access: 400 W PEP on HF through 70cm, 120 W on 50.0-50.5 MHz and all bands from 23cm upward, 30 W on 50.5-52 MHz and 50 W on 4m. 2200m (emission class A1A only) and 630m (A1A/F1A/G1A/J2A; contests not allowed) are F-only; 60m is F-only at 15 W EIRP; duplex links are not allowed on 50.5-52 MHz and 4m. In the 30m band the regulation prints two overlapping rows (10.100-10.150 kHz, contests not allowed; and 10.140-10.150 kHz, max 500 Hz bandwidth); they are encoded here as two tiled segments with both restrictions applying to 10.140-10.150 kHz. Amateurs are secondary users in several segments and must additionally respect RDI-published temporary primary-user notches (e.g. around major events).
